annotations.title: Fit a design to its size

description:
Put a design made before the product was chosen onto its cart line, fitted to the size the customer chose, and show it before paying.

Call this once the customer chose a delivery option for a line whose `design_id`
came from `catalog_configure_product`: pass the `line_id` and the chosen
`offer_ids`, one per cart line. When the size differs, the design is laid out
again, which takes about a minute. `adapted: false` means it already fitted and
nothing changed. If `catalog_configure_product` reported an Unmet Constraint for a
line, the call fails with `UnmetConstraintUnansweredError` until the customer
answers; if they accept the line as configured, call again with
`unmet_accepted=true`. The payment link refuses a line whose design still needs
this step (`AdaptStepRequiredError`).

The result shows the design on its size (`product_label`, `thumbnails`,
`design_url`). Share `design_url` as a markdown hyperlink and the thumbnails. When
the design card is displayed, it shows the previews with "Looks good" and "Change
something", so don't paste the link or describe the images. Ask whether it looks good; for a change, call
`design_chat` with `design_id`.

Returns a job — poll until SUCCEEDED.
name: design_adapt

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Fit a design to its size
